newsitem.title: ITALY: BASKETBALL-NBA IN WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP PROMISE.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-NBA IN WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP PROMISE.

text.p: At least 10 of the 12-strong U.S. squad for next year's world basketball championships in Greece will be NBA players, NBA deputy commissioner Russ Granik promised on Wednesday.
"The plan is to name the 10 players some time next fall (autumn) and I think those 10 will all be NBA players," he told reporters covering Europe's Final Four club championship.

He added: "As we've done with preceding international events at a senior level over the last several years, two spots will wait till the spring and those could be players coming out of college or they could also be NBA players."
The same could also be said for the 2000 Olympics in Sydney, Granik added. "You can expect to see the very, very best teams that together the NBA and U.S. basketball can create."
Such assurances will be especially welcome in basketball-crazy Athens where preparations are already under way for the world championships there next summer.
Meanwhile, the U.S. is one of nine countries, including Iran, who have announced their "strong intention" to bid to hold the men's 2002 world championships.
Bids have to be in by July 31 and the decision will made at the end of November, FIBA, the international federation, said on Wednesday.
Granik also confirmed that the new women's NBA in the U.S. would start on June 21 with eight teams, ending with the championship on August 30.

He said: "Our goal is to start small -- we're only playing a 28-game season -- but in a way which we know will make sense from a business standpoint in the hopes of building long-term the sport of women's basketball at a professional level in a way that it has now grown on the collegiate level."
